_about: Routing eval cases. must: every one has to be picked. any: at least one has to be picked. accept: fine to pick, not required. avoid: wrong pick. via, when a case sets it, is the expected hand-off; otherwise the hand-off is judged from the router's own valid picks by step 3 of the route skill. See evals/routing/README.md.

cases.request: Design a six-frame sword attack with anticipation, contact and recovery timing, and tell me how much hit-stop to use.
I need a 32x32 sprite sheet for a knight with idle, run and attack. What frame counts, palette size and atlas padding?
Model my soft currency: list the sources and sinks and tell me whether my shop prices will cause inflation.
Write branching shopkeeper dialogue in Ink with line IDs and a length limit per line.
Two codex entries disagree about the year the war ended. Find the canon contradictions and log the retcon.
Write a dissolve effect and an animated menu backdrop as GLSL shaders.
Compose a seamless overworld loop with layered stems that add intensity when combat starts.
Make NES-style jump and coin pickup sounds and give me the sfxr parameters.
Set up a Godot 4 project with typed GDScript and a sensible scene tree for a top-down game.
Our Bevy game stopped compiling after a version upgrade. Help migrate our systems and schedules.
Players rubber-band in my 60 Hz shooter. Design client prediction and lag compensation.
Design Glicko-2 skill rating with queue widening at low population and fair handling of parties.
My character tunnels through thin walls when moving fast. How do I stop it?
Design a versioned save file with migrations and atomic writes so a crash can't corrupt it.
The game hitches every few seconds. Here is a profiler capture; is it CPU or GPU bound and what's the frame budget?
Build a GitHub Actions pipeline that exports my Godot game headless and uploads the build to Steam.
Audit my subtitles, input remapping and colour-blind options against the Game Accessibility Guidelines.
Rewrite my Steam short description, pick tags and plan my Next Fest demo.
Plan a think-aloud playtest with eight players and show me how to analyse what they did versus what they said.
Design behaviour trees and a sight-and-hearing perception system for stealth guards.
Find free footstep and UI click sounds that I can ship in a commercial game.
Find a dialogue addon for Godot 4 with an MIT licence.
Build an MCP server that exposes my level editor's tools to an AI assistant.
How much will LLM-driven NPC chat cost per player-hour, and how do I cap it with quotas?
Generate dungeons from room templates with a seed and validate that every one can be completed.
Review my metroidvania's ability gating and how much backtracking it costs the player.
Is the prestige loop in my idle game paced well, and how should offline progress work?
Set the tile size, camera angle and depth sorting rules for an isometric game.
I want the PS1 look: vertex jitter, affine texture warp and low-res dithering. Write the style sheet.
Which NASA API gives near-Earth asteroid data, do I need a key, and what are the rate limits?
Implement patched conics and time warp for a Kerbal-style orbit simulation without precision drift.
What do Space Apps Challenge judges look for, and how do I scope a game for the two-day hackathon?
Make the triage and outbreak mechanics in my hospital sim medically plausible.
Are we close to the Claude usage limit? Should this plan run at a lower effort level?
Check my 1920s Chicago setting for anachronisms and point me to primary sources.
Model fatigue, form and injury risk for players in my football manager sim.
My platformer's jump feels floaty. Tune coyote time and the jump buffer.
cases.note: Three agents own part of jump feel. Any one is a fair first pick.

cases.request: Is the font licence on our UI pack OK for a commercial release?
cases.note: law-civics-expert covers law as game content, not licences for the project.

cases.request: Educational solar-system game for a classroom: map the learning objectives and use real planet data.
I need a pixel-art hero end to end: a character brief, a sprite sheet and a walk-cycle timing chart.
cases.note: design + art inside creative, so via creative-lead; adding pixel-art-stylist (knowledge) makes it shop-steward.

cases.request: Add rollback netcode to my Unity fighting game.
cases.note: multiplayer + engines inside technical, so via technical-lead; adding fighting-expert (knowledge) makes it shop-steward.

cases.request: Title screen package: a logo lockup, an animated parallax title screen with press-start timing, and a theme loop.
cases.note: screens-effects + sound inside creative, so via creative-lead with any of the accepted extras too.

cases.request: An LLM-driven tavern keeper in Unreal Engine 5 who remembers the player and answers only from our lore bible.
cases.note: ai-integration + engines inside technical, so via technical-lead; adding npc-designer or lore-keeper (creative) makes it shop-steward.

cases.request: Browser multiplayer card game: choose between Phaser and PixiJS for it, and pick the realtime transport.
Review the core loop of my city-builder and make the zoning and traffic behave like a real city.
cases.note: genres + domains inside knowledge, so via knowledge-lead.

cases.request: Free-to-play mobile RPG: design a fair battle pass and the telemetry events to measure retention.
cases.note: Both sit in production/production, so no lead is needed unless rpg-expert (knowledge) is added.

cases.request: I want a pixel-art metroidvania in Godot. Where do I start?
cases.note: The README example.

cases.request: Farming sim on Roblox: make crop growth realistic and save player farms with DataStores.
Horror game: tune the dread pacing and set the ambient sound direction and mix rules.
Voxel survival-crafting game in Unity: set voxel budgets and meshing rules, and review the recipe tree.
A hacking minigame that is believable but safe, and a threat model for our real leaderboard backend.
Tower defense for the browser: tune the wave economy and pick between Phaser and PixiJS.
Find Unreal-ready modular sci-fi corridor kits on Fab and tell me the licence tier.
Ask the composer for a boss theme with a stinger for phase two.
cases.note: The user named a specialist, so route straight to them.

cases.request: Design a courtroom cross-examination mechanic that follows real trial procedure.
cases.note: Law as game content, not legal questions about the project. game-designer is a fair extra: the request asks to design a mechanic.

cases.request: Implement controller focus navigation for my pause menu.
Draw 9-slice panels, button states and an icon set for the HUD.
Our tycoon game's profit and loss model lets players go infinitely into debt. Fix the cash flow rules.
cases.note: In-game finance, not how the game itself makes money.

cases.request: My game runs fine on my PC but it's choppy on the Steam Deck.
cases.note: h cases are worded the way players and new developers talk, not the way the catalog does.

cases.request: People keep quitting in the first five minutes and I don't know why.
Someone is posting impossible scores on our online leaderboard.
I need the bad guys to feel smart without feeling unfair.
We ship in three weeks and the feature list is way too long. What do we drop?
My buttons work with a mouse but a gamepad can't reach half of them.
We want to put the game out in Japanese and German. What is going to break?
Our Discord is on fire because the last update nerfed everyone's favourite weapon.
Can I put a real football club's badge and kit in my game?
The moon level should have the right gravity, and you shouldn't be able to hear explosions out there.
Make my 3D game look like a Saturday-morning cartoon.
Players lose all their progress when the power cuts out mid-game.
My game stutters whenever a big wave of enemies spawns in at once.
cases.note: A symptom, not a discipline. Naming the bound behind a hitch is the performance engineer's job; pooling the spawns may then fall to a programmer.

cases.request: My friend is colour-blind and can't tell the red team from the green team in my game.
I'm making a game for kids. Is it OK to let under-13s make accounts and chat with each other?
cases.note: game-legal-advisor lists child privacy and education-expert lists COPPA questions. law-civics-expert is law as game content.

cases.request: My game's download is 4 GB and most of that is pictures. How do I shrink it without it looking worse?
cases.note: Texture compression and packing are in technical-artist's description; the word 'pictures' points at the art makers instead.

cases.request: When I alt-tab out and back in, the game sometimes freezes. How do I write this up so the programmer can actually fix it?
cases.note: The ask is a reproducible bug report, which qa-tester's description names, alt-tab included. 'Freezes' points at performance-engineer, a fair extra but not the owner.

cases.request: I've never coded. Should I make my small 2D platformer in Godot, Unity or GameMaker?
cases.note: Choosing between engines is technical-director's 'engine, language and backend choices'. Each engine specialist covers one engine, so they are fair extras, not the owner.

cases.request: There are two of us and we keep arguing about what the game even is. The idea changes every week.
cases.note: Pillars and a dated decision log settle this; brief-keeper is the specialist people forget.

cases.request: Before we spend a month building it, how do we find out if a grappling hook is even fun?
The boss fight has a lot of flashing lights. Could that hurt anyone?
cases.note: Photosensitivity. vfx-artist lists flash safety; accessibility-specialist covers sensory needs.

cases.request: Do I have to tell people on my Steam page that I used AI to make some of the art?
cases.note: Steam's AI disclosure is named in both AI specialists' descriptions. 'Steam page' points at store-page-marketer, who writes the page but does not own the rule.

cases.request: We're submitting to Xbox certification next month. How do we know we'll pass?
cases.note: qa-lead lists certification readiness, release-manager console cert windows, accessibility-specialist cert prep.

cases.request: A zombie virus in my city game should spread through the population like a real epidemic.
cases.note: healthcare-expert lists outbreak mechanics and epidemiology; biology-ecology-expert lists disease spread.

cases.request: We used an AI clone of a famous actor's voice for a joke cameo. Is that going to get us in trouble?
cases.note: voice-director lists AI voice consent; game-legal-advisor gives legal information on the project. law-civics-expert is law as game content.

cases.request: A mock-trial game for a high-school civics class that teaches due process and fits in one 45-minute lesson.
cases.note: Two domain experts in the same department, so direct; adding game-designer makes it shop-steward.

cases.request: Design the puzzle rules for a bus-route game set on real city maps, using real timetable data.
cases.note: urban-planning-expert lists GTFS data. With puzzle-expert the picks stay in knowledge (knowledge-lead); with game-designer they span divisions (shop-steward).

cases.request: Design a nurse-shift game where patient flow and staffing are realistic but it's still fun to play.
cases.note: A domain expert alongside a designer.

cases.request: Our co-op survival game launches on Steam in a month. We still need servers to host it, a store page, and a crafting tree that isn't a grind.
cases.note: Three departments in three divisions. survival-crafting-expert lists recipe trees and economy-designer crafting costs, so either covers the grind.

cases.request: Mobile puzzle game: controls you can use with one thumb, a one-time price with no ads, and tiles that colour-blind players can tell apart.
Horror game in Unreal 5: a monster that tracks you by the noises you make, the direction for a creepy ambient soundscape, and a PS1-era look.
cases.note: Hearing-based tracking is perception (game-ai-engineer); horror-expert lists monster AI, so either fits.

cases.request: Should my basketball game use sim or arcade controls, and is a franchise mode worth the extra scope?
cases.note: sports-science-expert models athletes, not game modes or controls.

cases.request: In my bridge-building game a wooden plank holds 20 tonnes. Are my material numbers anywhere near real life?
cases.note: Real-world plausibility of numbers, not a collision or solver bug.

cases.request: Players say the late game of my RTS drags and one unit type beats everything. Review the pacing and the roster.
cases.note: defense-strategy-expert is real military logistics and wargaming, not RTS balance.

cases.request: We're about to launch. Go through every third-party sprite, font and plugin we used and list each licence with proof.
cases.note: An audit of assets already in the game; the scouts find new ones.

cases.request: Cut a 60-second launch trailer from our gameplay footage: shot list, music cues and what to capture.
How much real money should a premium skin cost in gems, and is our limited-time starter pack a dark pattern?
cases.note: business-finance-expert keeps tycoon and trading sims correct; it does not price the game itself.

cases.request: Players hack their save files to give themselves max level. Should I sign or encrypt our saves?
cases.note: t cases are traps: the obvious keyword points at the wrong agent, or a request looks multi-part but is one specialist's job. Here 'hack' points at cybersecurity-expert, which is hacking as game content.

cases.request: In my rhythm game the music slowly drifts out of sync with the notes after about a minute.
cases.note: Music-gameplay sync is in rhythm-expert's description. The composer writes the music; drift is not a composition problem.

cases.request: Loading into each level takes 40 seconds on console.
cases.note: IO-bound loading (performance-engineer) or asset streaming (engine-programmer); 'level' is a red herring.

cases.request: Set up cloud saves through Steam so players can carry on from their PC on a Steam Deck.
The guards in my stealth game spot the player instantly, even through walls.
cases.note: Perception is classic game AI. physics-programmer is a fair extra for line-of-sight collision filtering. Nothing here needs an LLM.

cases.request: Set up my Godot game properly: folder layout, a global game-state autoload, signal naming rules, and a web export I can put on itch.io.
cases.note: Looks like four jobs; all are in godot-specialist's description. web-engine-specialist is for Phaser-style frameworks and itch-scout finds assets.

cases.request: Before we translate the game: how do we get all the text out of the code, how much extra room does German need, how do we spot missing translations, and which fonts work for Chinese?
cases.note: Looks like four jobs; all are in localization-lead's description.

cases.request: Plan season 3: the event calendar, the battle pass track, and how often to run double-XP weekends without burning players out.
cases.note: Looks like three jobs; season cadence, event calendars and battle pass structure are all in live-ops-designer's description.
